reviews.name: Priya Nair
reviews.text: Ten years of build-up paid off. The final battle had my whole theatre cheering, and the farewells hit harder than I expected.

reviews.name: Lucas Moreau
reviews.text: Three hours long, but it never drags. The time-travel middle act is fan service in the best possible way.

reviews.name: Hana Sato
reviews.text: A satisfying ending if you've followed the series. Newcomers will be lost, but this film clearly isn't made for them.

reviews.name: Marcus Bell
reviews.text: Fun and colourful with a genuinely creepy villain, though the jokes undercut some of the emotional moments.

reviews.name: Ananya Iyer
reviews.text: Jane's return was the highlight for me. The screaming goats wore thin after the third time.

reviews.name: Tom Riley
reviews.text: Not as tight as the previous Thor film, but a breezy, good-looking watch on a lazy evening.

reviews.name: Ethan Walker
reviews.text: That long single-take chase sequence is worth the watch alone. Relentless from start to finish.

reviews.name: Tanvir Hossain
reviews.text: Great action, thin story. Fun to see Dhaka on screen, even if it's mostly being blown up.

reviews.name: Nina Petrova
reviews.text: Gritty and well choreographed. The quieter moments between the two leads land better than expected.

title: Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery

reviews.name: Sophie Turner
reviews.text: Clever, colourful and full of twists. Benoit Blanc is a joy every time he opens his mouth.

reviews.name: Aditya Kulkarni
reviews.text: The midpoint reveal completely reframes the first half. I immediately wanted to rewatch it.

reviews.name: Elena García
reviews.text: Not quite as tight as the first film, but the satire of rich tech types is very sharp.

reviews.name: Ryan Mitchell
reviews.text: Big, loud and globe-trotting. The villain is clearly having the time of his life.

reviews.name: Divya Pillai
reviews.text: The Prague tram fight is a highlight, but the plot is forgettable once the credits roll.

reviews.name: Jakub Novák
reviews.text: Stylish action with not much underneath. A decent popcorn movie for a Friday night.

reviews.name: Ashley Grant
reviews.text: Three huge stars bantering through a globe-trotting heist. Silly, but the chemistry carries it.

reviews.name: Marco Bianchi
reviews.text: Lots of twists, some of which make no sense at all. Still an easy, breezy watch.

reviews.name: Kiran Patel
reviews.text: Fun enough, but it feels like a mix of a dozen better heist films.

reviews.name: Michael O'Brien
reviews.text: A slow, sad, reflective gangster epic. The last half hour is quietly devastating.

reviews.name: Varun Desai
reviews.text: Three and a half hours is a lot, but the performances make every scene worth it.

reviews.name: Laura Schmidt
reviews.text: Masterfully made, though the de-aging effects pulled me out of it a few times.

reviews.name: Jessica Moore
reviews.text: Funny and frustrating in equal measure. The dinner scene near the end really stuck with me.

reviews.name: Arnav Gupta
reviews.text: The satire is not subtle at all, but the cast is clearly having fun with it.

reviews.name: Henrik Nilsen
reviews.text: Some sharp moments, but it hammers the same point for far too long.

reviews.name: Emma Clarke
reviews.text: Charming and energetic. The fourth-wall breaks make Enola feel like a friend you're solving cases with.

reviews.name: Riya Sen
reviews.text: A great family watch. Fun mystery, lovely costumes, and a lead who's easy to root for.

reviews.name: Pablo Fernández
reviews.text: Light and enjoyable, if a little long. The fight scenes are surprisingly good.

reviews.name: Kevin Park
reviews.text: A feel-good time-travel adventure with a surprising amount of heart about fathers and sons.

reviews.name: Sneha Reddy
reviews.text: The kid actor steals the show. The action is fine, but the family scenes are the best part.

reviews.name: Thomas Müller
reviews.text: Feels like an 80s Spielberg movie with modern effects. Easy Sunday afternoon viewing.

reviews.name: Amanda Lopez
reviews.text: Tense from the first scene. The blindfolded river journey had me holding my breath.

reviews.name: Rajesh Kumar
reviews.text: A great premise, and not showing the creatures was the right call.

reviews.name: Ingrid Berg
reviews.text: Gripping in parts, but the ending felt a little too neat for me.

title: All Quiet on the Western Front

reviews.name: Maximilian Koch
reviews.text: Brutal and unforgettable. That three-note score still gives me chills.

reviews.name: Samuel Wright
reviews.text: One of the most powerful anti-war films ever made. Not easy to watch, but essential.

reviews.name: Ishaan Malhotra
reviews.text: The cinematography is stunning, which makes the horror of the trenches hit even harder.

reviews.name: Rebecca Hall
reviews.text: Painfully honest. The argument scene is some of the best acting I've ever seen.

reviews.name: Nandini Rao
reviews.text: Neither character is the villain, and that's what makes it so sad and so real.

reviews.name: Julien Blanc
reviews.text: Quiet, funny in unexpected places, and heartbreaking. Bring tissues.

reviews.name: Tyler Brooks
reviews.text: The opening car chase through Florence is pure chaos in the best way.

reviews.name: Aman Verma
reviews.text: Explosions everywhere, story nowhere. Switch your brain off and it's fun.

reviews.name: Giulia Romano
reviews.text: Exhausting editing. Some great stunts are buried under constant cuts.

reviews.name: Sofia Martinez
reviews.text: Season one is gripping and uncomfortable in a way that stays with you. Clay carries every single episode.

reviews.name: Rahul Mehta
reviews.text: Started strong, but the later seasons stretched the story far thinner than it needed to be.

reviews.name: Emily Carter
reviews.text: Tough to watch at times. Worth it for the performances, but go in prepared for very heavy themes.

reviews.name: Jonas Weber
reviews.text: Every episode ends on a hook. The multilingual cast makes life aboard the ship feel chaotic and real.

reviews.name: Isabel Costa
reviews.text: Moody, beautiful, and confusing in a good way. A real shame we only got one season.

reviews.name: Arjun Rao
reviews.text: The ending raised more questions than it answered, but the atmosphere is unlike anything else.

reviews.name: Megan Brooks
reviews.text: Funny, warm, and surprisingly moving. Debbie steals every scene she's in.

reviews.name: Kavya Reddy
reviews.text: I knew nothing about wrestling and still loved it. The half-hour episodes make it very easy to binge.

reviews.name: Daniel Okafor
reviews.text: A brilliant ensemble cast, and the 80s costumes and soundtrack are a treat from start to finish.

reviews.name: Chloe Martin
reviews.text: A cosy kind of spooky. The key powers are creative, and Keyhouse itself feels like a character.

reviews.name: Vikram Singh
reviews.text: Season one is the strongest. The family drama gets in the way of the magic later on.

reviews.name: Lena Fischer
reviews.text: A good weekend binge with my younger siblings. Not too scary, but still properly tense.

title: Money Heist: Korea – Joint Economic Area

reviews.name: Min-jun Park
reviews.text: Moving the heist to a reunified Korea is a clever twist, and Berlin is excellent in this version.

reviews.name: Neha Kapoor
reviews.text: If you've seen the Spanish original, this follows it closely. Still fun, just with fewer surprises.

reviews.name: Carlos Ruiz
reviews.text: Tight and fast-paced. The cat-and-mouse scenes between the Professor and Woo-jin are the best part.

reviews.name: Oliver Hughes
reviews.text: Feels like the comic come to life. The episode with Death is one of the best hours of TV I've seen.

reviews.name: Aisha Khan
reviews.text: Gorgeous visuals, and the quiet, distant performance as Dream is exactly right.

reviews.name: Mateo Rossi
reviews.text: Slow in places, but the standalone episodes are fantastic and worth the wait.

reviews.name: Grace Kim
reviews.text: The Crows are the real stars. I'd happily watch a whole show of just Kaz, Inej and Jesper.

reviews.name: Rohan Das
reviews.text: Great world-building and costumes, and Kirigan makes a very convincing villain.

reviews.name: Freya Larsen
reviews.text: Season two rushes through a lot of story, but it's still an enjoyable fantasy adventure.

reviews.name: Jake Morrison
reviews.text: I grew up with these kids. The finale wrapped everything up, and I'm not ashamed to say I cried.

reviews.name: Meera Joshi
reviews.text: The 80s vibe, the soundtrack, the friendships. Season four in particular is incredible.

reviews.name: Sven Andersson
reviews.text: The seasons got longer and bigger, not always better, but it's still an absolute must-watch.

reviews.name: Isla Thompson
reviews.text: Dry, weird, and very funny. The dance scene at the Rave'N lives rent-free in my head.

reviews.name: Pooja Sharma
reviews.text: A fun mystery with great gothic style. Enid and Wednesday's friendship is the heart of the show.

reviews.name: Lucas Silva
reviews.text: Season two goes darker and more ambitious. Some episodes drag, but the finale makes up for it.

reviews.name: Hannah Lee
reviews.text: Joe's narration is creepily addictive. You end up rooting for him and hating yourself for it.

reviews.name: Siddharth Menon
reviews.text: Season one is a masterclass in tension. Later seasons get wilder but stay entertaining.

reviews.name: Clara Dubois
reviews.text: The London season was a fun change of pace, though I saw the big twist coming.

reviews.name: Tomasz Kowalski
reviews.text: As a fan of the books, season one's monster-of-the-week episodes felt just right. Jaskier's song is stuck in my head forever.

reviews.name: Rachel Adams
reviews.text: The jumping timelines in season one confused me at first, but it clicks by the end.

reviews.name: Anjali Verma
reviews.text: Great sword fights and creatures. The later seasons lost some of the magic for me.

reviews.name: Felix Braun
reviews.text: The most carefully plotted show I've ever watched. Every detail pays off by the final episode.

reviews.name: Sara Lindqvist
reviews.text: You need a notebook to keep track of the family tree, but it's absolutely worth it.

reviews.name: Nikhil Bose
reviews.text: Haunting atmosphere and a near-perfect ending. Watch it in German with subtitles.

reviews.name: Ji-woo Han
reviews.text: Brutal, emotional and impossible to stop watching. The marbles episode broke my heart.

reviews.name: Olivia Bennett
reviews.text: Childhood games turned into a nightmare. The set design is unforgettable.

reviews.name: Faisal Rahman
reviews.text: A sharp critique of debt and inequality wrapped in a thriller. Later seasons don't quite match the first.

reviews.name: Charlotte Evans
reviews.text: Lavish costumes, juicy gossip and string covers of pop songs. Pure escapist fun.

reviews.name: Shreya Nair
reviews.text: Season two is my favourite. The Sharma sisters brought so much warmth to the show.

reviews.name: Amélie Laurent
reviews.text: Gorgeous to look at, though the romance formula gets a little predictable each season.
